AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To examine the effect of a system of expedited review of critically ill patients in the Emergency Department (ED) on ED length of stay (LOS) and Intensive Care Unit (ICU) outcomes.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital comparing two 12-month periods before and after implementation of a 'Code ICU' system of expedited review of critically ill patients in the ED. All adult ED to ICU admissions were included. Separate analyses were performed for patients intubated prior to ICU admission.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 622 and 629 patients were included in each time period. During the intervention period more patients had ED LOS<240min in both the total [199 (32.0%) vs. 243 (38.6%), P=0.014; adjusted OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.14-2.25] and intubated cohorts [145 (51.2%) vs. 172 (61.9%), P=0.011; adjusted OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.16-2.36]. 'Code ICU' intubated patients had a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU LOS and hospital LOS compared to non-'Code ICU' intubated patients.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: A system of rapid review of critically ill patients in the ED was associated with reduced ED LOS and improved ICU outcomes.
